We have mass spec: m/z 193.1103 (M+? likely molecular ion). Proton NMR shows signals: 1.20 d (3H) typical ethyl CH3; 2.85 d (2H) maybe CH2 attached to aromatic? 3.09 qdd (1H) maybe CH of ethyl? 3.81 s (3H) methoxy; aromatic 7.15 ddd (2H) and 7.92 ddd (2H) suggests para-disubstituted benzene (AA'BB') pattern. So aromatic ring with two substituents para to each other. Substituents: one is methoxy carbonyl? Actually 3.81 s (3H) likely OCH3 of methyl ester. 1.20 d (3H) and 3.09 qdd (1H) and 2.85 d (2H) maybe ethyl group attached to aromatic? But ethyl would give quartet (CH2) and triplet (CH3). Here we have 1.20 d (3H) not triplet. So maybe isopropyl? 1.20 d (3H) suggests methyl coupled to a single proton (CH). 3.09 qdd (1H) is that CH coupled to methyl (J~7) and also to CH2 (6.9). 2.85 d (2H) maybe CH2 attached to aromatic (benzylic) coupling to CH? So overall side chain: O-CH2-CH(CH3)-? Actually 2.85 d (2H) could be CH2 attached to aromatic and to CH (coupling 6.9). So side chain is -CH2-CH(CH3)-? The CH is also coupled to OCH3? No.

We also have methoxy at 3.81 s (3H) likely OCH3 of methyl ester attached to carbonyl on aromatic ring (para to side chain). So structure: methyl p-ethyl? Wait side chain is maybe -CH2-CH(CH3)-? Could be -CH2-CH(CH3)-? attached to aromatic via CH2. So overall substituents: para-methoxy carbonyl (COOCH3) i.e., methyl ester (COOCH3) attached to aromatic (para). And para side chain is -CH2-CH(CH3)-? maybe -CH2-CH(CH3)-? but what is terminal? Could be -CH2-CH(CH3)-? maybe -CH2-CH(CH3)-? (no further). That is isobutyl? Actually isobutyl is -CH2-CH(CH3)2 (two methyls). Here only one methyl. So it's sec-butyl? sec-butyl is -CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3. Not match.

Our NMR: 1.20 d (3H) J=7.1, suggests methyl coupled to CH (quartet). But we have CH as qdd (1H) at 3.09 with J=7.1,6.9,6.9. So CH couples to methyl (7.1) and to CH2 (6.9). CH2 appears as d (2H) at 2.85 coupling 6.9 to CH. So side chain is -CH2-CH(CH3)-? The CH is attached to O? chemical shift 3.09 suggests attached to heteroatom (maybe O). Could be -O-CH(CH3)-CH2- attached to aromatic? But O-CH would be around 3.5. 3.09 maybe attached to aromatic? benzylic CH2 is ~2.8, CH attached to aromatic maybe ~3.0 if attached to O? Not sure.

Mass: 193.1103. Let's compute possible formula. If we have aromatic ring C6H4 (para disubstituted). Add methoxy carbonyl: CO2CH3 = C2H3O2? Actually methyl ester attached to aromatic: -COOCH3 adds C2H3O2 (plus carbonyl carbon). So total C8H3O2? Wait aromatic carbon attached to carbonyl carbon part of ring? The substituent is -C(=O)OCH3 attached to ring, adds C2H3O2 plus carbonyl carbon already counted? The carbonyl carbon is part of substituent, not ring. So adds C2H3O2. So far C6H4 + C2H3O2 = C8H7O2? Actually C6H4 + C2H3O2 = C8H7O2? Wait H: 4+3=7. Yes C8H7O2.

Side chain: -CH2-CH(CH3)-? attached to ring via CH2. That side chain formula: CH2-CH(CH3)-? The terminal maybe CH3? But we have only one methyl. So side chain is -CH2-CH(CH3)-? The CH attached to something else maybe H? Actually CH is attached to CH2 and CH3 and maybe H (makes CH). So side chain formula: C2H5 (CH2 + CH + CH3) = C2H5? Wait CH2 (CH2) = C1H2, CH (CH) = C1H1, CH3 = C1H3 total C3H6. But we have only C2? Let's count: CH2 (C1H2), CH (C1H1), CH3 (C1H3) total C3H6. So side chain adds C3H6. So total formula C8+3= C11, H7+6=H13, O2. So C11H13O2. Compute exact mass: C11=132.000, H13=13.101, O2=31.989 = 177.09. Not 193. So missing something.

Maybe side chain includes another carbonyl? Could be ethyl ester? But we already have methyl ester. Maybe the side chain is ethoxy? Actually 1.20 d (3H) could be methyl of ethoxy (CH3CH2O-). Ethoxy group gives quartet at ~1.2 (triplet?) Actually ethoxy CH3 appears as triplet ~1.2, not doublet. So doublet suggests methyl attached to CH (not CH2). So maybe it's isopropyl group attached to aromatic via carbonyl? But we have carbonyl already.

Let's compute mass for C12H14O3? mass ~ 210. Not.

Let's try to deduce formula from mass 193.1103 (likely M+). Use typical atomic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, O 15.994915. Let's guess formula C10H14O3: mass = 10*12=120 +14*1.007825=14.10955 +3*15.994915=47.984745 total =182.0943. Too low.

C11H14O3: 132 +14.10955+47.9847=194.0943 close to 193.11? Slight high. C11H12O3: 132+12.0939+47.9847=192.0786. Slight low. C10H12O4: 120+12.0939+63.97966=196.0736.

Our mass 193.1103 suggests maybe C11H13O2? compute: 132+13.1017+31.9898=177.0915 too low. C12H13O2: 144+13.1017+31.9898=189.0915. C12H13O3: 144+13.1017+47.9847=205.0864.

C10H13O3: 120+13.1017+47.9847=181.0864.

Maybe includes chlorine? But no.

Let's compute exact mass for C11H13O3: 132+13.1017+47.9847=193.0864 close to 193.1103 difference 0.024. Could be C11H13O3 with one extra H? C11H13O3 mass 193.086. Our observed 193.110, difference 0.024 (~124 ppm). Could be C10H9O4? 120+9.0704+63.9797=193.0501 diff 0.06.

Maybe includes nitrogen? C10H13NO2: 120+13.1017+14.0031+31.9898=179.0946.

Better to compute using tool get_formula_from_smiles for candidate.

We have candidate SMILES: CCOC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)C(C)CC earlier validated true. That is ethyl ester? Actually CCOC(=O) is ethyl ester attached to aromatic, plus side chain is C(C)CC (isopropyl ethyl?). Let's compute formula via tool.
